as_told.title: Shape-recovering foil debris at the crash site

plain: A witness to a reported 1996 UFO crash near Varginha, Brazil, says he picked up a piece of the wreckage and that it sprang back into shape whenever he bent it. If true, the craft was made of a material unlike anything ordinary. The witness is Carlos de Souza, who says he found the crash. He tells Michels himself that when he handled 'this foil or this sheet,' it 'regained its shape.' Michels retells it on several episodes. He calls the material 'light, tinfoily' and says it would 'immediately go back into its original shape, like some sort of memory metal.' He says this sounds 'exactly like the crash material at Roswell,' the famous 1947 crash in New Mexico. On another episode, Michels links it to what Bob Lazar, a man at the center of a long-running UFO story, describes. A surgeon named Italo Venturelli also points to 'the testimony of the guy who saw the spacecraft, picked up a piece with his hand,' but does not mention the shape-returning.
